label: John B. Alexander
narrative: Alexander is the retired Army colonel who spent the late 1980s trying to find the UFO programme from inside the government, with credentials that should have worked, and reported that he could not find it. A Special Forces officer turned Los Alamos National Laboratory programme manager for non-lethal weapons, and previously involved in the Army's INSCOM psychoenergetics work, he convened in the 1980s an interagency group he called the Advanced Theoretical Physics working group, drawing senior people from CIA, DIA, the services and the national laboratories to determine whether a compartmented UFO effort existed. His conclusion, stated repeatedly since, is that he found no such programme - a finding that cuts against this board's premise and is recorded here in full for exactly that reason. What his account does establish is that the search happened, that it was conducted by cleared senior people, and that the answer they got was the same answer David Grusch got in 2019: the programme, if it exists, does not answer to people who ask through channels. Alexander then joined NIDS as a board member from 1995, working alongside Puthoff, Kelleher and Vallee on Bigelow's private version of the same inquiry.
